summary: Both harnesses natively export OTel metrics and logs via OTLP/HTTP with env/config-only setup (no persistent config edited). Claude Code accepts OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp but emits zero trace payloads in this capture -- traces are documented as Beta and were empty in practice. Codex natively exports traces as well as metrics and logs, with per-turn/per-session spans and correlation ids (conversation.id, thread.id, turn.id). Prompt content is redacted by default in both harnesses and only appears when an explicit prompt-logging flag is set (OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1 for Claude Code, otel.log_user_prompt=true for Codex); this was verified with unique canary tokens per run. Numeric rate-limit/headroom data (remaining requests, reset windows) was not found in either harness's export: Claude Code has no rate-limit metric or attribute at all, and Codex emits only an opaque counter event (kind=codex.rate_limits on the codex.websocket.event metric) marking that a rate-limit websocket message arrived, with no limit/remaining/reset values attached.

method.sink: stdlib Python HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:4318 saving each raw OTLP/HTTP POST body to a file, one server per protocol variant (http/json for both harnesses so bodies are plain JSON, no protobuf decoding needed)
method.isolation: git worktree /projects/dev/_wt/agentops-otel-spike on branch evidence/native-otel-signals from origin/main; no edits to ~/.claude/settings.json or ~/.codex/config.toml -- all OTel config passed via environment variables (Claude Code) or `codex exec -c otel....=` overrides (Codex)
method.models: claude --model haiku; codex default model (gpt-6-astra) via codex exec, no model override needed since codex exec has no offline/free tier
method.canary_method: each run used a freshly generated unique marker token (prefixed for this work item, suffixed with a timestamp and a per-run letter) embedded in the user prompt; raw captures were grepped for the exact token to confirm presence/absence per run

harnesses.name: Claude Code

invocation.command: claude -p <prompt> --model haiku --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence [--allowedTools Bash for the tool-call run]

harnesses.notes: OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp was accepted (no error, no startup warning) but zero POSTs landed on /v1/traces across three runs (plain reply, tool-call reply, prompt-logging reply). Claude Code's own docs mark the traces exporter 'Beta'; observed behaviour is consistent with it being either unimplemented for the CLI-headless (-p) path or gated behind something this run did not trigger. Session correlation for metrics/logs is via session.id (a UUID) plus user.account_id/user.email/organization.id -- no span/trace ids observed anywhere. cost_usd on the api_request log event is the closest thing to spend telemetry; there is no field resembling remaining budget, quota, or a rate-limit window. Sensitive identifiers present by default (no prompt-logging needed): user.email (plaintext), user.account_id, user.account_uuid, organization.id, session.id, terminal.type; host OS/arch also appear as resource attributes but no absolute filesystem paths were observed.

harnesses.name: Codex CLI

invocation.command: codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --json -c otel.exporter.otlp-http.endpoint=... -c otel.exporter.otlp-http.protocol=json -c otel.trace_exporter.otlp-http.endpoint=... -c otel.metrics_exporter.otlp-http.endpoint=... [-c otel.log_user_prompt=true for the second run] --ephemeral <prompt>

key_attributes: kind (e.g. codex.rate_limits, as an opaque event-kind label on codex.websocket.event)
signals.rate_limit_data: partial: a codex.websocket.event data point can carry attribute kind=codex.rate_limits, meaning a rate-limit websocket message was received, but no numeric remaining/limit/reset value is attached to that or any other metric

names: conversation_starts (unnamed body, event.name attr not consistently set)
api request/response events (auth.*, duration_ms, success, endpoint)
token usage events (input_token_count, output_token_count, cached_token_count, reasoning_token_count)
prompt/user-input event (attribute key 'prompt', redacted by default)
(and ~90 more internal spans for tool/skill/mcp setup)
signals.canary_with_prompt_logging: not directly checked on trace spans (canary was confirmed via the log signal only); span attributes observed carry no prompt-text field, only token counts and code-location metadata

harnesses.notes: Codex exposes three independently configurable exporters (otel.exporter for logs, otel.trace_exporter, otel.metrics_exporter), each accepting otlp-http{endpoint,protocol=binary|json} or otlp-grpc{endpoint}, set only via -c overrides in this spike -- ~/.codex/config.toml was never touched (real CODEX_HOME used read-only for auth; no otel keys written there). metrics_exporter defaults to an internal 'Statsig' exporter unrelated to the OTLP sink; nothing about that default sends data to our sink unless overridden, and it was overridden here. Prompt-content behaviour mirrors Claude Code: the 'prompt' log attribute is the literal string '[REDACTED]' unless otel.log_user_prompt=true, verified with a canary token that appeared only in the prompt-logging run. Traces cover a full session/turn lifecycle in fine detail (per-function instrumentation, not just top-level request/response), correlated by conversation.id/thread.id/turn.id. Sensitive identifiers present by default: user.email (plaintext), user.account_id, conversation.id, app.version/host info; code.file.path attributes on spans leak internal source file paths of the Codex binary itself (not user filesystem paths).

conclusions.native_traces_cover_sessions: Codex: yes, natively and in detail (per-turn spans with token usage and timing, correlated by conversation/thread/turn id). Claude Code: no -- OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp is accepted but produced zero trace payloads in three runs including one with a tool call, consistent with the 'Beta' label in its docs; Claude Code's session/turn story lives only in its log events (api_request, tool_result, etc.) correlated by session.id, not in spans.
conclusions.native_rate_limit_windows: No for either harness. Claude Code emits no rate-limit-shaped metric, attribute, or log field at all. Codex emits one opaque marker (codex.websocket.event{kind=codex.rate_limits}) that only proves a rate-limit message arrived over its websocket, with no remaining/limit/reset numeric fields exported alongside it.
conclusions.prompt_content_default_off: Yes for both. Verified experimentally: a canary token in the prompt was absent from all captured OTLP payloads under default settings and present only after setting OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1 (Claude Code) or otel.log_user_prompt=true (Codex). Both harnesses use a literal '<REDACTED>' / '[REDACTED]' placeholder in the redacted case rather than omitting the field.
sensitive_identifiers: user.email (plaintext account email; present by default on nearly every Claude Code and Codex signal)
session.id (Claude Code) / conversation.id, thread.id, turn.id (Codex) -- stable-per-run identifiers that could correlate activity across signals and across time if retained
terminal.type and host.arch/os.type/os.version (Claude Code resource attributes) -- low sensitivity but host-identifying
code.file.path on Codex trace spans -- internal Codex source paths, not user data, but still an implementation-detail leak worth scrubbing before wide distribution of raw traces
